title: Top floor, please!
paragraphs: Have you ever been in a lift with the big cheese in your company? It happened to me a couple of times. And did I take advantage of the situation to deliver my elevator pitch? Not a chance. He was surrounded by people buttering him up all the way to the top floor!

Lifts have an interesting history. Today, the more important you are, the higher you live or work. Penthouses have fantastic views for boardrooms and living rooms. But it hasn't always been that way. Before the days of lifts, richer people would often prefer to live on the ground floor. Poorer people lived on the upper floors – and they had to use the stairs.

In any case, whatever your pay grade, the confined space of a lift makes for an awkward encounter. It's hard not to notice the uneasiness of a group of strangers in a confined space who have no time to develop any kind of bond. But if marketing people have their way, that's all going to change.

Jason Whale, sales manager at Elevators Ltd, says: "It's a very anxious experience the time you spend in a lift. If you have things around you, you take away that awkwardness. We all look at our phones sometimes or look down at the floor. Well, surely it's better to look at advertisements on the walls…"

He sees a lot of potential in this box in which we spend a few minutes every day. Whale explains: "As technology becomes slimmer and cheaper, there are so many different ways to enhance a lift with light boxes, with moving images, with television screens! It becomes quite exciting for us, and hopefully a little bit more interesting for the people who use lifts."

Who knows what the lifts of the future will look like? Perhaps they will become the places where everybody wants to be. Time for a business meeting? Ready to party? Come on everybody, let's get into the lift!

vocabulary.entry: big cheese /bɪɡ tʃiːz/ n. 大人物；核心掌权者（短语）【口语表达】
vocabulary.example: He is the big cheese of the whole department.
vocabulary.translation: 他是整个部门的核心人物。

vocabulary.entry: a couple of /ə ˈkʌpl əv/ 数个；几次（短语）【口语表达】
vocabulary.example: I met my manager a couple of times last week.
vocabulary.translation: 我上周偶遇经理好几次。

vocabulary.entry: take advantage of /teɪk ədˈvɑːntɪdʒ əv/ 利用；趁机把握（短语）
vocabulary.example: You should take advantage of every learning chance.
vocabulary.translation: 你应当把握每一次学习机会。

vocabulary.entry: elevator pitch /ˈelɪveɪtə pɪtʃ/ 电梯演讲；简短商务自荐（短语）
vocabulary.example: A perfect elevator pitch helps you leave a good impression.
vocabulary.translation: 简洁的电梯自荐能帮你留下好印象。

vocabulary.entry: not a chance /nɒt ə tʃɑːns/ 绝不；毫无可能（短语）【口语表达】
vocabulary.example: Not a chance will I agree with this silly idea.
vocabulary.translation: 我绝对不会认同这个荒唐的想法。

vocabulary.entry: butter up /ˈbʌtə ʌp/ 讨好；阿谀奉承（短语）【口语表达】
vocabulary.example: Many staff try to butter up their leaders.
vocabulary.translation: 不少员工会刻意讨好上级。

vocabulary.entry: penthouse /ˈpenthaʊs/ n. 顶层豪华公寓；顶楼套房
vocabulary.example: The celebrity lives in a riverside penthouse.
vocabulary.translation: 这位名人住在河畔的顶层豪宅。

vocabulary.entry: boardroom /ˈbɔːdruːm/ n. 董事会议室；高层会议室
vocabulary.example: The meeting will be held in the main boardroom.
vocabulary.translation: 会议将在主董事会议室举行。

vocabulary.entry: pay grade /peɪ ɡreɪd/ 薪资等级；薪酬档位（短语）
vocabulary.example: Your pay grade will rise with your work performance.
vocabulary.translation: 工作表现越好，薪资等级越高。

vocabulary.entry: confined /kənˈfaɪnd/ adj. 狭窄的；封闭受限的
vocabulary.example: A confined space easily makes people feel nervous.
vocabulary.translation: 封闭狭小的空间容易让人紧张。

vocabulary.entry: make for /meɪk fɔː(r)/ 造成；促成（短语）
vocabulary.example: Long silence makes for a strange atmosphere.
vocabulary.translation: 长久的沉默会营造诡异的氛围。

vocabulary.entry: uneasiness /ʌnˈiːzinəs/ n. 局促；不安
vocabulary.example: Strange silence brings obvious uneasiness.
vocabulary.translation: 陌生的沉默会带来明显的局促感。

vocabulary.entry: bond /bɒnd/ n. 情感联结；人际纽带
vocabulary.example: Daily communication builds a close bond.
vocabulary.translation: 日常交流能建立紧密的人际联结。

vocabulary.entry: have one's way /hæv wʌnz weɪ/ 随心所欲；如愿行事（短语）【口语表达】
vocabulary.example: You cannot always have your way in teamwork.
vocabulary.translation: 团队合作中不能凡事随心所欲。

vocabulary.entry: awkwardness /ˈɔːkwədnəs/ n. 尴尬；窘迫难堪
vocabulary.example: Small talk can break the awkwardness in a lift.
vocabulary.translation: 闲聊可以化解电梯里的尴尬。

vocabulary.entry: anxious /ˈæŋkʃəs/ adj. 局促的；焦虑不安的
vocabulary.example: He feels anxious when staying with strangers.
vocabulary.translation: 和陌生人共处时，他会感到局促。

vocabulary.entry: potential /pəˈtenʃl/ n. 潜力；发展前景
vocabulary.example: The media space in lifts has huge commercial potential.
vocabulary.translation: 电梯传媒空间拥有巨大商业潜力。

vocabulary.entry: slim /slɪm/ adj. 纤薄的；轻薄简约的
vocabulary.example: Modern display screens are slim and durable.
vocabulary.translation: 现代显示屏轻薄且耐用。

vocabulary.entry: enhance /ɪnˈhɑːns/ v. 提升；美化；优化
vocabulary.example: Colorful screens enhance the indoor environment.
vocabulary.translation: 彩色屏幕优化了室内环境。

vocabulary.entry: light box /laɪt bɒks/ 灯箱广告；发光展示牌（短语）
vocabulary.example: Bright light boxes attract people's attention quickly.
vocabulary.translation: 亮眼的灯箱能快速吸引人们目光。

vocabulary.entry: moving image /ˈmuːvɪŋ ˈɪmɪdʒ/ 动态影像；流动画面（短语）
vocabulary.example: Moving images are more attractive than static posters.
vocabulary.translation: 动态影像比静态海报更具吸引力。

vocabulary.entry: television screen /ˈtelɪvɪʒn skriːn/ 电视屏幕；显示屏（短语）
vocabulary.example: The television screen in the lift plays short videos.
vocabulary.translation: 电梯内的电视屏幕会播放短视频。

vocabulary.entry: encounter /ɪnˈkaʊntə(r)/ n. 偶遇；碰面邂逅
vocabulary.example: An unexpected encounter may cause embarrassment.
vocabulary.translation: 突如其来的碰面可能引发尴尬。

sentences.chinese: 穷人则住在更高的楼层——因此他们不得不使用楼梯。

sentences.english: In any case, whatever your pay grade, the confined space of a lift makes for an awkward encounter.
sentences.chinese: 无论如何，无论你的薪资级别如何，电梯狭小的空间必然导致尴尬的偶遇。
